title: Power Automate: generate documents from SharePoint document generation forms
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and data policy control are supported. A minor completeness issue remains: the checklist asks administrators to review library permissions and licence assignments that have no corresponding controls-table rows.

claims.claim: Generate document from form creates documents by mapping input data to document generation template fields.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The action saves generated documents to a SharePoint library.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the action returns the generated document with metadata such as location and status.
claims.quote: The action works by mapping input data to template fields and returns the generated document along with file metadata such as location and status.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives contracts, invoices, letters and reports as example uses.
claims.quote: This capability supports scenarios such as creating contracts, invoices, letters, or reports using structured templates and form-driven inputs.

claims.claim: The capability involves makers building flows and content managers creating and configuring document generation forms.
claims.quote: Content manager (template creator) - Creates and governs templates and forms. They define the document structure, required fields, and conditional rules

claims.claim: The source template must be a Word document in .docx format.
claims.quote: The source document must be a Microsoft Word document (.docx format).

claims.claim: Form creation starts from the Forms command in a SharePoint document library.
claims.quote: In a SharePoint document library, select Forms from the command bar.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Generated documents are stored in the library folder associated with the form by its creator.
claims.quote: Open the folder that's linked with the form. Each generated document is stored here with the submitted values merged into the template.

claims.claim: Submitting a document generation form automatically creates a document with the submitted values merged into its template.
claims.quote: When a user submits a form, the system automatically generates a new document from the template with the submitted values merged into the appropriate fields.

claims.claim: Form submitted (Preview) triggers a flow when a form is submitted.
claims.quote: Form submitted (Preview) triggers a flow when a form is submitted, so you can start workflows such as approvals or notifications.

claims.claim: Get form metadata (Preview) retrieves the form structure for mapping responses to fields.
claims.quote: Get form metadata (Preview) retrieves the form structure, so you can map responses to fields without manual configuration.

claims.claim: The structured document generation page does not name a licence for form submitters.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "structured document generation" "licensing"; "Generate a document from a form" "license". Read the structured-generation page's prerequisites and requirements: the licence prerequisite names content managers, not submitters.

claims.claim: The structured document generation page gives no price.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint "structured document generation" "licensing"; "document generation" "SharePoint" "credits". Read the structured-generation page in full; it lists a Copilot licence prerequisite but no price.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy > Pre-built connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business reaches connector classification.
claims.quote: In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy. ... In the Pre-built connectors page ... select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Confidential -Connectors <connector objects> adds or moves connectors to a policy's Business group.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName 7b914a18-ad8b-4f15-8da5-3155c77aa70a -Connectors $connectorsToClassifyAsBusiness -Classification Confidential Adds the MSN Weather connector to the Business group of the policy.

claims.claim: Data policies control which other connectors flows in the policy's environments may combine with SharePoint.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: The data policy page says SharePoint cannot be placed in the Blocked group.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level data policy steps require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policy steps require Power Apps Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse-database exception.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies in environments with a Dataverse database instead require the System Administrator role.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Learn does not document a tenant switch specifically for document generation forms or their three Power Automate items.
claims.quote: Searched: "Set-SPOTenant" "DocGen"; SharePoint "document generation forms" "admin". Read structured-generation, connector pages and Copilot get-started; searched Set-SPOTenant for DocGen, forms and document generation; no specific tenant switch.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the governance checklist asks administrators to review.
claims.quote: Review Edit permissions on the libraries ... Check which Microsoft Copilot licences are assigned ... Review the destination libraries for who can open the generated documents. The sole table row concerns connector combinations.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps to review library Edit permissions and Copilot licence assignments, and the After rollout step to review generated-document access, have no corresponding controls-table rows.
